documents.title: Surveillance cystoscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY - flexible cystoscopy, 3-month surveillance. Date 07/08/2025.
History: high-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma, TURBT 3/18 and 4/22, BCG induction x6 completed 6/17.
Findings: right lateral wall scar well healed. No papillary or flat lesions. Both orifices normal with clear efflux.
Impression: no recurrence.
Plan: maintenance BCG (3 weekly instillations) to start late August; cystoscopy again in 3 months.

reports.text:

OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - surveillance. Date of service 07/29/2025.
Esophageal adenocarcinoma cT3 N0, definitive chemoradiation 2024, complete response January.

We see his PCP has referred him to our hematology colleagues for new anemia with a high globulin level; that visit is 8/11 here.

documents.title: Hematology consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY - new consultation. Date of service 08/11/2025.

Referred for anemia with an elevated globulin.

HPI: 71 year old man previously treated for esophageal adenocarcinoma (chemoradiation 2024, complete response) and high-grade T1 bladder cancer (TURBT and BCG 2025). For about two months he has had fatigue, headaches and blurred vision, and recently began bleeding spontaneously from the gums and nose.

Other history: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, permanent AF on warfarin, prior mild stroke, AAA s/p EVAR with cholesterol embolism, inclusion body myositis, PAD, GERD, hyperlipidemia.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol succinate, warfarin, aspirin, atorvastatin, omeprazole. NKDA.
Family: paternal uncle with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia; father ruptured AAA; mother diabetes, macular degeneration; brother hypertension.
Social: retired construction foreman; 40 pack-years, quit 2017; red wine most evenings.

Exam: pale. Fundoscopy shows engorged retinal veins. Distal sensory loss in both lower extremities. No palpable lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly.

Labs today: hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, MCV 89 fL, platelets 150,000/uL. SPEP with a monoclonal IgM spike, M-protein 3.6 g/dL; IgM 4,850 mg/dL. Serum viscosity elevated at 4.6 cP.

Procedure today: bone marrow aspirate and biopsy, posterior iliac crest, tolerated well (INR checked; warfarin not held, held pressure).

Assessment: monoclonal IgM paraproteinemia with symptomatic hyperviscosity (headache, visual blurring, retinal venous engorgement, mucosal bleeding) and anemia - most consistent with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, marrow pending.

Plan:
- Plasmapheresis urgently: first session tomorrow 8/12, second 8/14.
- Marrow results expected within the week; definitive therapy to follow.
- Avoid transfusion before plasmapheresis.
- He will continue warfarin; any significant bleeding to the ED.

events.reason: Bone marrow results and treatment plan

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy, posterior iliac crest.
MICROSCOPIC: Marrow infiltrated by a population of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes and plasma cells. Flow cytometry shows a clonal B-cell population. Clonal lymphoplasmacytic cells constitute 15% of marrow cellularity.
reports.conclusion: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, 15% marrow involvement, consistent with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia in the setting of an IgM paraprotein.

documents.title: Hematology follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY - follow-up. Date of service 08/18/2025.

Bone marrow 8/11: 15% clonal lymphoplasmacytic cells. With the IgM monoclonal protein this confirms Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.

Plasmapheresis 8/12 and 8/14 completed. Serum viscosity after: 2.3 cP. Headaches gone, vision clearer, no bleeding since the first session.

Diagnosis: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia with hyperviscosity, treated with plasmapheresis.

Treatment plan: bendamustine-rituximab, six cycles every 28 days starting 9/2. Viscosity and IgM monitored for flare after rituximab, with repeat plasmapheresis if needed. Weekly CBC early on. His warfarin can continue with closer INR checks by his PCP's office. We have asked urology to defer maintenance BCG during chemoimmunotherapy; they agree.
Thank you for the prompt referral.

High-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma s/p TURBT x2 and BCG induction. Maintenance BCG on hold during bendamustine-rituximab for Waldenstrom.
Findings: healed right lateral wall scar. No tumor.
Plan: cystoscopy every 3 months; revisit maintenance BCG after chemoimmunotherapy.

documents.title: Hematology treatment visit
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY. Date of service 11/25/2025.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia on bendamustine-rituximab, cycle 4 day 1 today.
After 3 cycles: M-protein 1.5 g/dL (3.6 at diagnosis). No hyperviscosity symptoms; no IgM flare requiring plasmapheresis. Fatigue for a few days after each cycle. No infections.
Plan: continue to 6 cycles; response assessment after completion.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD. Date of service 02/15/2026.

CC: fever, burning with urination.

HPI: 71 year old man with a history of bladder cancer (TURBT, BCG) and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (last bendamustine-rituximab 1/20/2026) with 3 days of fever, dysuria and urinary frequency. No flank pain. No vomiting.

PMH: also esophageal adenocarcinoma s/p chemoradiation, AAA s/p EVAR, permanent AF on warfarin, prior stroke, DM2, HTN, HLD, PAD, IBM, GERD.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, warfarin 5 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, omeprazole 20 mg. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 88, T 38.4 C.
Exam: uncomfortable, nontoxic. Suprapubic tenderness. No flank or CVA tenderness. Heart irregularly irregular. Lungs clear.

Data: urinalysis with pyuria and bacteriuria. Creatinine 1.1. WBC 12,000. Urine culture sent. Abdominal ultrasound from last month reviewed: aneurysm present, no change in size.

ED course: ceftriaxone 1 g IV. Tolerating oral fluids, fever down.

Impression: urinary tract infection (cystitis with fever), recent chemoimmunotherapy.
Disposition: discharged. Cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily for 10 days. Antibiotic may raise INR - INR with PCP this week. Return for rigors, flank pain, vomiting, confusion. PCP follow-up in 1 week. Culture results will be sent to PCP.

documents.title: Hematology end-of-treatment visit
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY. Date of service 03/10/2026.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, completed bendamustine-rituximab x6 (9/2/2025-1/20/2026). E. coli UTI in February treated as an outpatient.
M-protein 0.7 g/dL (3.6 at diagnosis): partial response. No hyperviscosity symptoms. Hemoglobin improving.
Plan: observation, no maintenance therapy. Labs and visit every 3 months. From our standpoint urology may resume maintenance BCG when they judge it appropriate; we suggest waiting until counts are fully recovered.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY - surveillance cystoscopy. Date 07/14/2026.
High-grade T1 urothelial carcinoma, TURBT 3/2025 and 4/2025, BCG induction 5-6/2025, maintenance deferred during and after WM therapy.
Findings: no recurrence. Healed scar right lateral wall.
Plan: cystoscopy every 3 months through the second year. We discussed resuming maintenance BCG; he prefers to continue surveillance alone for now, which is reasonable given clear cystoscopies.
